thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected: spike of GPU OOMs during prefill on prod-west-us-gamma. Multiple container restarts on nodes gpu-pool-3a. Auto-generated pager PD-98321.
anya: seeing continuous OOMs from prefill path, looks tied to very large user prompts (concatenated transcripts). Repro on a single node: prefill alloc tries ~28GB and hits CUDA OOM.
mike: I'm pulling logs now — can you paste an example request id?
anya: request id abc12345, model rwd-gpt-13b, prompt length ~420k chars (~120k tokens) — they were doing long transcript ingestion + system prompt.
rahul: here's the extract from kube logs for container rwd-runtime-7f8: ```
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.00 GiB total capacity; 24.50 GiB already allocated; 300 MiB free; 24.10 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/prefill.py", line 198, in run_prefill
    kv_cache = model.prefill(tokens)
  File "/app/runtime/model.py", line 412, in prefill
    outputs = self.forward_prefill(chunk)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 88, in alloc
    raise CudaOOMError("CUDA out of memory")
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
--- container restart triggered by OOM killer ---
```
jessie: :wave: I'm on-call for prod; paging inbound. Is there any immediate customer impact?
liz: We've got 2 support tickets tied to streaming failures and one webhook delivery failure. Customers reported truncated responses and reconnect loops. No major data loss, but degraded UX for chat product.
mike: Metrics: prefill OOM rate jumped at 03:11 UTC, error % from 0.02% -> 1.8% in 3m. Autoscaling kept replacing crashed pods but churn caused increased latency for other routes.
anya: immediate mitigation idea: 1) temporarily reject prefill requests above a configured token threshold for the prod model family, 2) route long-context requests to low-memory fallback (quantized small model) with best-effort note, 3) enable aggressive prefix eviction and fallback to CPU decode for extremely long prefill.
rahul: I can push a config change to runtime config store to cap prefill tokens to 75k for rwd-gpt-13b. That should stop the worst ones. Prep a runtime hotpatch to return 413 for too-large prefill.
jessie: Do it. Also add a short-term admission control that enforces `max_prefill_tokens` per request and increments a counter for telemetry.
ops-bot: Deploy started: config/runtimes/prod/rwd-gpt-13b set max_prefill_tokens=75000 by rahul (deploy id d-9923). Rolling restart will proceed with maxUnavailable=1.
mike: Rolling restart in progress. Noting that pods still crash during prefill in-flight; we need to ensure in-flight requests are drained. Suggest `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --grace-period=30 --force` on affected nodes to stop churn.
rahul: Draining nodes now and adding eviction policy for KV cache. Also toggled `prefill_timeout_ms=15000` so long prefill attempts abort early.
anya: Patch ready for runtime: if prefill before token 2M attempts > allocated threshold -> raise early OOM and trigger soft-fallback to CPU or quantized model. I'll ship a small change that returns structured error with suggestion to truncate.
liz: Support note drafted: "We're seeing errors for very large prompts. We're applying throttles and fallbacks; to avoid interruptions, reduce prompt size or retry with trimmed context. Status updates will be posted to status.redwood.ai."
jessie: Status page draft posted (minor): "Partial service degradation for long-context generation affecting a subset of customers in US-West" — include ETA: 30m for mitigation window.
mike: After config rollout, OOM rate dropped to 0.12% in 10m. Pod restart rate reduced by 90%. Latency stable.
anya: Confirmed two customers still hit edge cases where prefill token count was computed incorrectly due to a pre-tokenization bug. Patch will be included in next patch; in-flight mitigation: rewrite tokenizer call to fail-fast and log token_count on reject.
rahul: Created follow-up ticket INF-4527 to add pre-tokenization sizing in the gateway. Also scheduled dedicated canary for long-prefill path to hit a canary node with increased logging.
ops-bot: Pager duty note: PD-98321 acknowledged by jessie; handoff scheduled to jessie->mike at 03:40 UTC.
jessie: Handoff to night oncall @mike in 25m. If anything spikes again, escalate to runtime-eng (anya) and infra (rahul).
liz: Customer comms: Sent an owner reply to tickets explaining mitigation and workaround; offered to assist with prompt truncation.
mike: Follow-ups: 1) add guard in gateway Reject if prefill token > 100k (return 413), 2) runtime to expose metrics per-request token_count, 3) add alert for prefill-ooms > 3/min.
anya: I'll PR the runtime patch and include unit test for token_count gating. ETA ~2h for full patch; short term changes live.
rahul: Ops notes: added Emergency K8s taint to gpu-pool-3a to prevent new scheduling of heavy prefills while we patch.
jessie: Marking incident as mitigated for now — continued monitoring. Will reopen if OOM rate > 0.5% or pod restarts spike.
incident-bot: Incident PD-98321 updated: state=mitigated, severity=minor, summary="GPU OOMs from very large prefill prompts caused container restarts; throttles and fallbacks applied; follow-ups created."
mike: Thanks team. Postmortem next steps: timeline, root cause (no prefill token guard + users concatenating transcripts), remediation (gateway gating, runtime early-fail, better telemetry), and customer impact summary for CSM. Assigning postmortem owners: anya (runtime), rahul (infra), liz (support).
anya: I'll start the postmortem doc and link here. Good job on quick mitigations. :thumbsup:
